_why: DEFECT-OAG-091 / loop-gate check 8. Declares which local containers belong to ROC and the MAX DISPATCH LIFETIME the reaper derives liveness from. Ownership is provenance (the compose file the container was started from), never a container-name list. Established 2026-08-18 after the loop-gate reported ROC NOT ESTABLISHED — which is not the same as clean: ROC's four emulator containers were undeclared, so an orphan wave would have accumulated unseen. The outage that preceded this left all four Exited(255) for 18h, invisible to any check.
_leaseTtlS: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE LEASE: unlike OagEventSource, ROC HAS NO LEASE WRITER. Its stack starts via `npm run local:up` (a bare `docker compose up -d`) with no `ddb-local-up` equivalent and no per-tier `assert-ours` renew hook, so NO ROC container ever gets a lease file. Consequence, stated plainly: the lease's absolute veto is unavailable here and age past leaseTtlS is the ONLY thing standing between a legitimately-running emulator stack and removal. That is why this value is 4h rather than OAG's 1h -- the ROC local stack is long-lived across a whole session's demo/E2E work (demo.sh waits on emulator readiness markers and the browser-driven E2E validation runs against the same stack), not per-tier like a DynamoDB Local. The missing lease writer is a REAL GAP, registered as its own defect rather than papered over here; when it lands, this should drop back toward the OAG value.
_minAgeS: Start/reap race floor: a container this young is immune regardless. The four emulators have a genuine cold-start chain (sql-edge -> servicebus-emulator, plus eventhubs-emulator and azurite), so the floor is above the OAG default to cover the whole chain coming up.
